messages:
ellie: Quick design review thread — API keys page. Focus: create / rotate / revoke flows, permission scaffolding, warning prominence, and keyboard/a11y nits. I threw a couple of mocks in the doc: https://redwood.design/keys-mock (tl;dr below) sam: Saw the mocks. Two quick things: 1) In the revoke modal the primary/destructive ordering is inconsistent with other modals. 2) The success state after rotation disappears too quickly — we lose keyboard focus and screen-reader announce. jordan: Re ordering — agreed. We should be consistent with the console pattern: primary action (Confirm) on the right, cancel on the left, and destructive styled red when the action is irreversible. Noticed earlier threads where we flipped this for compact modals. kai: Accessibility note: the revoke modal needs an explicit aria-role and live-region update on success. Right now NVDA reads nothing when the key is revoked. Suggestion: after revoke, set focus to the empty-state CTA and fire `aria-live="polite"` with message: \"Key revoked: You can restore from soft-delete for 7 days.\" ellie: Good call. UX question: should we show a hard warning banner above the form (inline) when revoking a key with active Dedicated assignments? Example copy from the mock: "This key is attached to Dedicated deployment X and will stop traffic immediately. Consider rotating instead." Too wordy? andrew: Keep it short. Maybe: "Active Dedicated routes will fail immediately. Consider rotating instead of revoking." Add a small link: "Show affected services" that toggles a list. jordan: Also propose a subtle affordance showing permission scope on the modal (read-only chips) so people don't accidentally rotate a key thinking it's low-impact. That should reduce accidental revokes. ellie: On rotate flow — product asks for a one-click rotate that swaps secret and keeps bindings. Engineering says we need a staged rollout: create new key, swap bindings, then soft-delete old key. Can we hide the steps but show a progress modal with steps and back button? sam: Progress modal is fine. Small UX nit: progress modal must be cancellable only before swap step, after that block. Add a bold step label: "Swapping bindings — this may interrupt traffic briefly". And in mobile view, keep text condensed. kai: Copy/contrast nit on the keys list: the permission chips have 3:1 contrast against the background when gray. Need >=4.5:1 for body text. Either darken chip text or add outline. aria-describedby should point to the role explanation. aria-bot: accessibility-scan: low-contrast detected on 2 elements: permission-chip, quiet-link. Recommendation: increase contrast or add icon to supplement color. ellie: Thanks aria-bot — can you attach the failing selectors to the design doc? aria-bot: attached: .perm-chip, .quiet-link (see doc comments). andrew: Empty state for keys page — proposing CTA copy: "Create your first API key" vs "Get started". Which is clearer for SSO orgs where keys might be created by admins only? jordan: Use explicit copy: "Create an API key". If user lacks permission, show disabled CTA with tooltip: "You need admin permissions to create keys. Contact your org admin." ellie: Good. Also UX for bulk revoke in the empty/soft-delete state: we need to prevent accidental bulk actions. Suggest: when selecting >5 keys, show a confirmation checkbox: "I understand revoking affects services" and require typing the org name for org-admins. sam: Strong agree. For bulk rotate we can show a smaller confirmation because rotating is less destructive. ellie: Final small copy suggestions for the revoke warning text (trying to keep it short): ``` Revoke API key This will immediately stop any services using this key. If you need to rotate, choose "Rotate" to keep continuity. ``` Keep the heading and one-line body, then a tertiary link: "Show services using this key". andrew: One more infra constraint: when we rotate keys we sometimes create a transient duplicate key ID (for bookkeeping). Product should avoid exposing that to users — make the modal show only friendly names and final status. ellie: Awesome, I'll update the mock: fix button ordering, add aria-live message, tweak copy, bump contrast on chips, and add progress modal state for rotate. I'll ping design review when ready. Thanks everyone :thumbsup: sam: +1 — also add a test case in playbooks: keyboard-only revoke -> confirm focus returns to list and screen-reader announces. jordan: Will add to QA. kai: I'll post a quick snippet later for the aria-live wrapper: ```
Key revoked: restored for 7 days
``` ellie: Perfect — thread closed unless more nits.
